title: A Semi‐Quantitative Yeast Complementation Platform for Characterizing Urea and Ammonia Transport
author: Stoib, Shojaei, et al.
materials: Saccharomyces cerevisiae deletion strain YNVW1 (Δdur3, Δura3)
Yeast Transformation Kit (Sigma Aldrich, cat. no. YEAST1)
Candidate protein HpUreI with point mutations A57C and L134C in pYES2 vector
Empty vector pYES2, as negative control
This section describes the preparation of chemically competent S. cerevisiae cells using the Yeast Transformation Kit 1 (Sigma Aldrich) according to the manufacturer's instructions.

This section describes the transformation of candidate plasmids into YNVW1 competent cells using the Yeast Transformation Kit 1 (Sigma Aldrich), with minor modifications to the manufacturer's protocol. Perform this step at least 2‐3 days before the assay to allow transformed colonies to grow on selection plates. For best comparability, transform all candidate plasmids simultaneously using the same batch of competent cells.

Saccharomyces cerevisiae deletion strain Sc18‐Δmep1‐3 (Δmep‐1‐3, Δura3; background: 31019b; full genotype in Table 1)Vectors encoding candidate proteins: HpUreI, HpUreI E177Q, and hAQP8 in pYES2 vector under the control of the GAL1 promoterEmpty vector pYES2, as negative controlAmmonia pH media at different pHs (4.0‐7.0; see recipe)Control medium, pH 6.0 (see recipe)
Perform the Basic Protocol with the following modifications to the indicated steps:

steps.title: Clean work area and equipment
steps.instruction: Clean all surfaces and equipment with 70% ethanol before and after use; work near a Bunsen burner or in a laminar‑flow hood; keep yeast‑related activities physically separated from other microbial work to maintain sterility and avoid bacterial contamination such as Escherichia coli.

steps.title: Inspect cultures for contamination
steps.instruction: Visually or with a cell counter examine all cultures and media for contamination; autoclave any contaminated samples, media, or waste immediately; prepared media may be stored refrigerated for several weeks but must be checked for contamination before use; autoclave all discarded cultures and liquid waste.

steps.title: Prepare chemically competent yeast cells
steps.instruction: Using the Yeast Transformation Kit 1 (Sigma‑Aldrich), follow the manufacturer’s instructions to generate chemically competent Saccharomyces cerevisiae cells; this preparation requires approximately two days.

steps.title: Transform plasmids into competent cells
steps.instruction: With the same Yeast Transformation Kit 1 (Sigma‑Aldrich) and minor modifications to the kit protocol, transform each candidate plasmid (HpUreI, HpUreI E177Q, hAQP8, and empty pYES2 vector) into YNVW1 competent cells; plate the transformed cells on selective media and incubate for 2‑3 days; perform all transformations simultaneously using the same batch of competent cells and start at least 2‑3 days before the assay.

steps.title: Inoculate liquid cultures from colonies
steps.instruction: On Day 0, pick individual transformed yeast colonies of the Sc18‑Δmep1‑3 (Δmep‑1‑3, Δura3) strain and inoculate them into the appropriate liquid medium (e.g., ammonia pH media at pH 4.0‑7.0 or control medium at pH 6.0) to start cultures; this step takes about ten minutes.
